newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Fuel up on prompt demand, crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Fuel up on prompt demand, crude.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps firmed late afternoon on Wednesday on strong crude prices and fresh prompt buying interest, traders said.
"Prompt physical buying from a trader is keeping the market up," one trader said.
April fuel oil swaps were last quoted $102.50/$104.00 per tonne, up sharply from Tuesday's $99.50/100.50.
Sources said April swaps traded earlier in the day at $102.00 and $102.50 per tonne.
Overnight May Brent crude closed up a hefty 75 cents to $20.25 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
April naphtha was last quoted at $24.60/$24.95 per barrel in thin trading, brokers said.
Gas oil also firmed late afternoon after a day of hectic physical trade on Tuesday where five cargoes totalling 750,000-tonnes traded at $27.00-28.60 per barrel, fob.
April gas oil was last quoted at $26.35/$26.50, up from Tuesday's $25.70/$25.80, brokers said.
Sources said market expectations are that the recent support from a local trader will continue at least until the end of this week.
The local trader has already bought around three million barrels since March 3.
Traders said the hefty rise was also due to expectations of sustained buying from the trader similar to that seen in the gas oil market since the start of March.
On Tuesday, the trader was bidding for a 20,000-tonne cargo at $100.00-tonne free-on-board against an initial offer at $101.00 from a major.
A second local trader attempted to buy the cargo offered by the major but do deals materialised.
Sources said the market took the second trader's intention to buy at the higher price as an indication of a fresh round of support for the fuel oil market. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3093)
